7. Its processors and amplifiers are specified by custom installers and integrated into bespoke home cinema and professional audio systems.
8. Its hardware platform is built around exclusive room optimization technology using a dedicated 3D measurement microphone to identify loudspeaker positions and analyze acoustic response.

points.name: Audio Foundry
points.description: Detroit collaborative platform accelerating in-vehicle audio prototyping for automakers using specialized design tools and physical test setups.
points.bullets:
A collaborative automotive audio technology platform and physical prototyping space that provides specialized equipment, design tools, and engineering services to help automakers and Tier 1 suppliers accelerate in-vehicle audio development. The organization bridges hardware and software, enabling manufacturers to test experimental speaker placements and new audio architectures before committing to production.
1. A developer tools and physical prototyping company whose platform engineers use to build, simulate and test in-vehicle audio systems in a physical demonstration environment.
2. Acoustic demonstration setups, specialized speaker configurations, and audio processing software integrated to visualize and prototype in-cabin acoustics.
3. Spatial audio, active noise cancellation, subwoofer size reduction, acoustic alignment and stabilization, and ultra-low frequency sound pressure generation.

points.name: Silentium
points.description: Israeli company developing active noise cancellation technology for automotive cabins.
points.bullets:
An audio software company that develops active noise cancellation and active sound management software, licensing it to automotive manufacturers and other industries to reduce unwanted noise and shape cabin acoustics.
1. An audio software developer whose active noise cancellation algorithms run on DSP cores and audio processors embedded in customers' automotive and industrial platforms.
2. Active noise control and road noise cancellation algorithms that generate anti-noise signals to attenuate unwanted sound in real time.
3. Active road noise cancellation, in-cabin noise reduction up to 1 kHz, personalized quiet zones, and active sound management for mechanical and industrial equipment.
4. Software and algorithms licensed for integration into audio voice processors, DSP platforms, and finished hardware cabinets.
5. Vehicle cabins, server and networking equipment racks, home appliances, and HVAC systems.
6. Automotive OEMs, semiconductor and audio processor companies, and industrial equipment manufacturers.
7. Its software is ported and integrated by DSP and chip vendors onto their platforms, which are then designed into vehicles by automakers.
8. It creates localized personalized quiet zones around individual occupants using active road noise cancellation rather than whole-cabin broadband suppression alone.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its software is integrated with Cadence Tensilica HiFi DSPs and AKM audio voice processors, and it is developing integrations with SonicEdge ultrasonic speaker arrays.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Software licensing and per-unit royalties.
Scale and maturity: An established company with multiple commercialized active noise control product lines.
Geography: Based in Israel, serving global automotive and industrial markets.
Beyond audio: It focuses entirely on active noise cancellation and sound management technology.

points.name: JL Audio
points.description: US audio manufacturer building subwoofers, speakers, and amplifiers for car and marine audio systems.
points.bullets:
A maker of finished audio equipment that designs, manufactures and sells car and marine speakers, subwoofers, amplifiers and signal processors for consumers and installers.
1. A consumer and car audio equipment maker that builds speakers, subwoofers and amplifiers sold as finished physical hardware for vehicles and boats.
2. The core technology consists of loudspeaker driver design using Dynamic Motor Analysis, voice-coil and elevated-frame cooling thermal management, and integrated digital signal processing built into amplifiers.
3. The equipment delivers high-fidelity bass reproduction, multi-channel sound amplification, signal conversion and digital signal processing for vehicle and marine sound systems.
4. Customers get the products as finished hardware, including vehicle-specific subwoofer enclosures, loaded subwoofer boxes, standalone speakers, amplifier chassis and wiring kits.
5. The products are used in cars, trucks, boats and marine vessels for aftermarket audio system upgrades and installations.
6. The company sells to consumers, vehicle owners, aftermarket car audio retailers and professional installers.
7. Its finished hardware products are retailed by car audio and consumer electronics dealers to end users for vehicle installation.
8. The company's approach is distinguished by vehicle-specific subwoofer enclosures engineered for fit and sound in specific vehicles alongside a focus on low-distortion, high-output bass.

points.name: Continental
points.description: German automotive technology company turning vehicle interior surfaces into speakers using compact vibrating actuators.
points.bullets:
An automotive audio systems supplier that develops surface-excitation audio technology, replacing conventional loudspeakers with compact actuators that vibrate vehicle surfaces, and provides software and engineering services to automakers.
1. A systems integrator and equipment maker that builds surface-exciting audio hardware and accompanying software, sold as integrated modules and engineering services implemented directly in vehicle interiors.
2. Actuators that excite existing vehicle surfaces to produce sound, combined with digital signal processing for sound design, noise cancellation, and spatial audio rendering.
3. Full-range and bass audio reproduction, active noise cancellation, seat-based sound zones, acoustic vehicle alerting, and immersive 3D audio playback.
4. Finished hardware components, licensed software algorithms, and engineering services integrated directly into vehicle platforms during development.
5. Car interiors across entry-level to premium trims, with demonstrated use in sports cars and electric vehicles.
6. Global automotive original equipment manufacturers.
7. Its integrated hardware and software systems are designed directly into vehicle platforms by automakers.
8. It replaces conventional loudspeakers with actuators that vibrate existing vehicle surfaces, reducing installation volume by up to 90 percent and cutting vehicle weight by up to 40 kilograms.

2. Digital signal processing and visual rendering algorithms that analyze audio signals and display level, loudness, vectorscope, real-time analysis and chart data against international standards.
3. Audio loudness measurement, level metering, audio analysis, vectorscope display, real-time analysis, mono-to-7.1 surround metering and loudness compliance monitoring.
4. Finished hardware units with touch screens and licensed software plug-ins.
5. Television and radio broadcast environments, mastering studios and professional audio production facilities.
6. Audio professionals, broadcasters and production facilities.
7. Its hardware units and plug-ins are used by audio professionals to measure and monitor audio signals during production and broadcast delivery.
8. Its plug-in interfaces are modeled directly on its hardware meter units, bringing hardware-style visual metering into software workflows.

points.name: ITU-R
points.description: Geneva-based standards organization defining global recommendations for audio broadcasting and loudness measurement.
points.bullets:
A standards body that develops radiocommunication standards and recommendations, including algorithms for measuring audio programme loudness and true-peak audio level, and file formats for international audio programme exchange, for broadcasters and the audio industry.
1. A standards body that publishes formal recommendations and file formats that define audio measurement algorithms and exchange metadata.
2. Mathematical algorithms for calculating integrated loudness in LUFS and true-peak audio levels, alongside specified metadata structures for long-form audio files.
3. Standardized measurement of audio programme loudness and true-peak audio level detection.
4. Published recommendation documents and standardized file format specifications.
5. Television broadcasting, radio broadcasting, and international audio programme exchange.
6. Broadcasters, regulators, audio equipment manufacturers, and software developers.
7. Its recommendations are implemented by equipment makers and software developers into their loudness meters and broadcast systems.
8. It defines the mandatory international standard algorithm for loudness measurement used globally to normalize audio levels.

2. CGI-like audio software using particle-based sound generation in 3D virtual spaces, integrating Higher Order Ambisonics, object-based audio rendering, and a spatial audio synthesis engine with MIDI-controlled spatial panning.

points.description: UK AI company developing generative audio models and codecs for sound production.
points.bullets:

It trains text-to-audio latent diffusion models and Transformer-based speech codecs on licensed and Creative Commons data. It licenses these models and API services to individual creators, developers, and enterprises.
1. An AI model developer whose generative audio and speech codec models run in the cloud behind an API and on-device on consumer-grade hardware.
2. The core technology consists of fast latent diffusion models operating on a semantic-acoustic autoencoder with frozen pre-trained text encoders, alongside Transformer-based speech coding.
3. It delivers text-to-audio generation, full song composition, sound effects generation, audio extension, audio editing, and high-quality low-bitrate speech coding.
4. Customers access the models through open-weight downloads, cloud APIs, a free web application, and a digital audio workstation plugin.
5. The technology is used in enterprise sound production environments, mobile devices, and digital audio workstations.
6. The company sells to individual creators, developers, enterprises, and organizations requiring commercial audio generation.
7. Its models are accessed directly by creators and developers and are licensed by enterprises for self-hosted commercial audio production.
8. It distinguishes its approach by emphasizing a legally sound footing through training on licensed and verified Creative Commons data while providing open weights for smaller models.

points.name: Kaldi
points.description: Open-source project providing building blocks for developers to construct custom speech recognition systems.
points.bullets:
An open-source developer tools project that provides a toolkit of audio algorithms and building blocks for engineers and researchers to construct custom automatic speech recognition systems from scratch.
1. A developer tools project whose toolkit engineers and researchers use to build their own speech recognition models, distributed as open-source software that can be compiled for embedded deployment on edge devices.
2. A traditional multi-stage automatic speech recognition pipeline combining feature extraction, acoustic modeling using Gaussian Mixture Models and Hidden Markov Models or neural networks, language modeling, and Weighted Finite-State Transducer-based decoding.
3. The toolkit delivers feature extraction, acoustic and language modeling, decoding, and streaming speech-to-text capabilities for custom systems, including specialized voice command recognition for edge devices.
4. Customers get the software as a free open-source toolkit licensed under the Apache 2.0 license, supplied with shell scripts that chain pipeline stages together.
5. The systems built with the toolkit are used in embedded deployments for offline edge usage and custom research applications for low-resource languages.
6. The project serves research teams, PhD students, and engineers needing fully custom automatic speech recognition systems.
7. The approach provides total control over every component of the recognition pipeline rather than offering an opaque, end-to-end model or commercial API.

3. Physical audio capture and playback, enabling wake-word detection and voice assistant functionalities when flashed with third-party software.
4. The company delivers finished hardware units and connectable microphone modules directly to users.
5. Do-it-yourself smart speakers, smart home hubs, and Bluetooth proxies.
6. Makers, technology enthusiasts, and smart home hobbyists.

points.name: Edge Impulse
points.description: Software platform helping developers build and deploy machine learning models for audio processing on edge devices.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that provides a platform for developers to build, train, and deploy machine learning models for audio processing on edge devices. The platform supports the entire machine learning workflow, from data acquisition to model design and deployment, offering specific audio processing blocks and learning algorithms. It enables on-device inference for microcontrollers, mobile devices, and single-board computers.
1. A developer tools company whose platform engineers use to build, train, and deploy their own ML models.
2. The platform uses digital signal processing blocks, neural network classifiers, and transfer learning models, optimized for edge performance using vector extensions, quantization, and a dedicated compiler to reduce memory footprint.
3. It delivers audio capabilities including keyword spotting, wake-word detection, environmental sound classification, cough detection, and speech, music, and noise distinction.
4. Customers get it through software development kits, exported libraries, and compiled models running on customers' devices.
5. The platform is used for offline voice-activated assistants, environmental sound identification, real-time healthcare cough detection systems, and continuous audio recognition on microcontrollers and mobile devices.
6. The organization sells to developers, machine learning enthusiasts, and engineers.
7. Its platform is used by developers to create machine learning models that are deployed onto low-power microcontrollers and neural decision processors from semiconductor companies.
8. It provides an automated tuner to suggest optimal combinations of digital signal processing and learning block parameters, and uses a dedicated compiler to significantly reduce the memory footprint of neural networks on microcontrollers.

A manufacturer of professional audio equipment that designs and builds digital mixing consoles, audio networking routers, and remote stage racks for the live sound market. The company produces low-latency audio mixing ecosystems and proprietary high-speed audio network protocols for touring, theatre, and installation applications.
1. A professional audio equipment maker that builds digital mixing consoles, stage racks, and network bridges sold as finished hardware.
2. Digital mixing engines with low-latency audio routing, integrated digital signal processing, and a proprietary high-speed audio network protocol carrying multichannel 24-bit, 96kHz audio over coax or fiber.
3. Digital audio mixing, multichannel audio networking and routing, network bridging to standards-based protocols, and wireless remote control and monitor mixing.
4. Finished hardware products, including digital consoles, stage racks, network routers, and expansion cards, alongside iPad and iPhone control applications.
5. Live sound touring, theatre productions, studio recording, and permanent audio installations.
6. Live sound engineers, theatre sound operators, recording studios, and audio installation professionals.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold through authorized distribution partners to professional audio engineers and installation integrators.
8. It combines proprietary high-speed, low-latency multichannel audio networking directly integrated with its own digital consoles and remote I/O ecosystem.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Integrates Waves SoundGrid interfaces and plug-ins into its consoles, and runs control applications on Apple iPad, iPhone, and Mac platforms.
Organization type: A privately held professional audio equipment manufacturer operating as two independent business units, one for consoles and one for immersive audio.
Business model: Hardware sales of digital consoles, stage racks, network bridges, and expansion cards.
Scale and maturity: A long-standing professional audio brand with heritage dating back to 1968, engineering and manufacturing its products in the UK.
Geography: Based in the UK, where it conducts product development, manufacturing, and brand management, selling its products globally through distribution partners.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus, split specifically between professional mixing consoles and immersive audio products.

3. Digital mixing, spatial audio, audio editing, networked audio routing, and signal processing.
4. Free downloadable software applications and finished hardware control surfaces and mixers.
5. Broadcast facilities, live events, and post-production studios.

8. Its approach is defined by tightly integrated, end-to-end audio workflows embedded within a broader video post-production ecosystem, rather than as a standalone audio solution.

points.name: Tascam
points.description: Japanese audio equipment manufacturer building recording interfaces and mixers for musicians.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional and consumer audio recording equipment that manufactures multitrack recorders, mixers, audio interfaces, portable field recorders and microphones for musicians, engineers and broadcasters.
1. An equipment manufacturer that builds finished audio hardware and integrated recording devices for studio, live and field capture.
2. Discrete component first-stage amplification circuits and constant current power supply circuits form its proprietary microphone preamplifier architecture, integrated into analog and digital recording devices.
3. Multitrack audio recording, analog mixing, analog-to-digital and digital-to-analog conversion, microphone preamplification, USB audio interfacing, DAW control and Dante connectivity.
4. The company delivers finished hardware products, including rackmount units, portable handhelds, desktop consoles and standalone microphones.
5. Its equipment is used in home studios, professional recording studios, live sound reinforcement, broadcasting facilities, podcasting setups and field recording environments.
6. The company sells directly to consumers, musicians, audio engineers and broadcast professionals.
7. Its finished hardware is sold to recording professionals and musicians through retail channels.
8. It introduced multitrack cassette recording to the consumer market and integrates mixing, recording and interfacing into single affordable desktop units.

2. Digital signal processing algorithms, including digital reverb, delay, and surround sound spatial rendering technologies.
3. Reverb generation, multi-effects processing, digital delay, immersive surround sound rendering, acoustic enhancement, and preamplification.

5. Recording studios, live venues, luxury cars, home theaters, and cinema installations.
6. Recording studios and musicians, live venues, automotive manufacturers, and home cinema consumers.

points.description: Software company providing audio middleware that drives speakers directly from microcontrollers.
points.bullets:

The organization licenses algorithms that generate pulse-width modulated audio signals directly from microcontrollers, paired with simple H-bridge hardware or dedicated amplifier chips, for automotive and embedded device manufacturers.
1. An audio software and IP licensor whose middleware runs on microcontrollers in embedded systems and automotive hardware.
2. Software algorithms that generate pulse-width modulated audio signals directly from a microcontroller to drive speakers through an H-bridge circuit without a traditional digital-to-analog converter.
3. Direct digital audio amplification, lossless digital audio playback, and component reduction for microcontroller-based sound systems.
4. Licensed IP and middleware.
5. Home appliances, in-vehicle devices, and general embedded audio equipment.
6. Automotive and embedded device manufacturers.
7. Its middleware is integrated by hardware developers into microcontroller-based embedded systems.
8. Replaces traditional digital-to-analog converter and low-pass filter circuits by driving speakers directly via a microcontroller and a four-transistor H-bridge.

4. Finished hardware and accompanying software platforms.

points.name: Ambient System
points.description: European manufacturer building public address, voice evacuation, and IP intercom systems for critical safety communications.

1. An equipment maker whose public address, voice evacuation, and IP intercom systems are sold as finished hardware and software installed in commercial facilities.
2. The systems combine audio routing, paging, and emergency alerting over IP networks to distribute live and pre-recorded voice instructions across large venues.
3. The organization delivers public address paging, voice evacuation, and IP-based intercom communication.
4. Customers get the offering as finished hardware and software products.
5. The products are used in airports, refineries, stadiums, tunnels, shopping centres, hospitals, railway stations, industrial plants, and office buildings.
6. The organization sells to facility operators, commercial enterprises, and institutional clients.
7. Its finished systems are installed directly into commercial facilities by integrators and operators.

points.name: Amina Technologies
points.description: UK company making invisible panel loudspeakers that hide inside walls and ceilings while turning surfaces into sound sources.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures invisible architectural loudspeakers using Distributed Mode Loudspeaker (DML) panel technology, producing flat-panel speakers that install flush into walls and ceilings to be hidden beneath plaster, paint or architectural finishes for custom install and commercial markets.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished architectural loudspeakers sold as physical hardware installed in building surfaces.
2. The core technology is Distributed Mode Loudspeaker (DML) architecture, where distributed-mode vibrations across a composite panel excite a surface to radiate diffuse sound, using a proprietary resin-impregnated cellulose pulp core panel with an anti-warp composite skin.
3. The speakers deliver wide audio dispersion at 150 degrees across a 60Hz to 20KHz frequency response, radiating from flat surfaces while remaining visually hidden beneath architectural finishes.
4. Finished hardware speakers in ceiling-grid and in-wall formats, available with custom vinyl or paint finishes.
5. Luxury residences, superyachts, commercial venues, hospitality spaces, premium architecturally designed homes and commercial ceiling installations.
6. Architects, designers, custom installers and commercial integration firms.
7. Its finished speakers are specified by architects and installed by custom integrators into architectural surfaces in residential and commercial building projects.
8. Its proprietary composite panel material and DML technology transform entire architectural surfaces into hidden high-fidelity sound sources finishable with stone, veneer, plaster, wood, leather or paint.

points.description: Chinese pro audio electronics company building professional power amplifiers and DSP equipment.
points.bullets:

1. An equipment maker that builds professional network power amplifiers with integrated 24-bit DSP audio processing, sold as finished hardware.
2. The core technology comprises Class H amplifier circuits and 24-bit DSP audio CMOS chips designed for long-distance audio signal transmission and control.
3. The equipment delivers audio power amplification, equalization, signal analysis, digital signal processing, frequency crossover, limiting and mixing.
4. Customers get it as finished hardware products and through custom-made OEM and ODM manufacturing arrangements.
5. The products are used in long-distance audio systems and professional installed audio setups.
6. The company sells to domestic and international equipment buyers, system integrators and custom OEM/ODM clients.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold directly into professional audio distribution and integration channels.
8. The approach is distinguished by integrating 24-bit DSP CMOS chips and computer control directly into Class H professional power amplifiers scaled across a wide power range.

points.description: US audio company building high-performance speakers and subwoofers for home theaters and immersive cinema sound.

A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures high-end loudspeakers and subwoofers for residential home cinema installations. The organization builds passive and active speakers featuring coaxial point-source designs and proprietary driver technology, calibrated for immersive audio environments. It supplies finished speaker hardware directly to custom installers and home theater integrators.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished loudspeakers and subwoofers sold as physical hardware installed in residential theaters.
2. Coaxial point-source driver geometries with concentrically aligned tweeters and midrange drivers, paired with proprietary speaker management technology for transient response and active subwoofer amplification.
3. Full-range sound reproduction, infrasonic bass extension down to 3 Hz, phase-coherent point-source radiation, and wide panoramic sound coverage for immersive cinema audio.
4. Finished passive and active loudspeakers and subwoofers, accompanied by published independent laboratory measurement data.
5. Residential home cinemas, dedicated theater rooms, and multiroom music systems.
6. Custom home theater installers, integration firms, and audiophile consumers seeking high-performance residential cinema hardware.
7. Its finished loudspeakers are specified and installed by custom integration firms into residential home cinema projects.
8. It emphasizes open scientific measurement data and coaxial point-source driver alignment to eliminate phase errors and comb filtering across all seating positions.

Organization type: A privately held audio equipment manufacturing company and a spin-off entity.

points.description: French research laboratory developing spatial audio algorithms for professional sound processors.
points.bullets:

8. The algorithms consolidate multiple spatialization techniques into a single processor capable of handling high channel counts natively.

points.description: AI startup developing conversational speech models that generate expressive audio directly.
points.bullets:

points.name: HILCodec
points.description: Neural audio codec compressing speech and music at low bitrates for real-time streaming.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer whose neural audio codec compresses clean speech, noisy speech, and music at low bitrates for real-time streaming applications. The organization provides an encoder-quantizer-decoder framework built on a time-domain Wave-U-Net architecture that operates with low computational complexity on standard CPUs.
1. An AI model developer whose neural audio codec runs in software on server CPUs.
2. A time-domain fully convolutional Wave-U-Net architecture utilizing depthwise-separable convolutions, residual vector quantization, and paired multi-resolution spectrogram and multi-filter bank discriminators.
3. Real-time neural audio compression and waveform reconstruction at bitrates from 1.5 to 9.0 kbps with a 24kHz sampling rate.
4. The codec achieves competitive audio quality at lower bitrates and with lower computational complexity and memory footprints than comparable neural audio codecs by employing a variance-constrained generator design and a distortion-free multi-filter bank discriminator.

2. Condenser and foil electret microphone transducer designs, vocoder and voder speech analysis and synthesis algorithms, and telephony transmission systems.
3. Acoustic transduction, speech synthesis and compression, audio amplification, stereophonic transmission and broadband digital line transmission.
4. Licensed intellectual property, patents and foundational hardware designs that were manufactured by partners.
5. Telecommunications networks, transatlantic cable systems, motion picture sound systems, laptops, hearing aids and cellular phones.
6. Telecommunications carriers, motion picture exhibitors and consumer electronics manufacturers.
7. Its patents and transducer designs were licensed to and manufactured by partners for integration into global communication devices and infrastructure.
8. It functioned as a vertically integrated, monopolistic corporate research facility that produced foundational, industry-standard inventions spanning hardware and algorithms rather than selling finished commercial products.

points.name: Google Research, Brain Team
points.description: Research lab blending interpretable signal processing with neural networks for high-fidelity audio synthesis.
points.bullets:
An AI model and software developer that builds a software library for audio synthesis, combining classic signal processing elements with modern machine learning methods for researchers and developers.
1. An AI model and software developer whose audio synthesis library runs as open-source software within a machine learning framework.
2. A differentiable digital signal processing library integrates interpretable signal processing modules with auto-differentiation-based neural networks within a machine learning framework.
3. The library enables high-fidelity audio synthesis, independent pitch and loudness control, blind dereverberation, room acoustics transfer, and timbre transformation between sources.
4. Customers get it as a publicly available open-source software library.
5. The organization sells to developers and researchers.
6. Its library is used by developers and researchers to build generative audio models.
7. The approach achieves high-fidelity audio generation without large autoregressive models or adversarial losses by combining interpretable signal processing modules with neural networks.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The software is built within the TensorFlow framework and was introduced by researchers at Google.
Organization type: The organization is a research team within a publicly traded technology company.

3. Immersive 3D audio decoding, far-field wake word recognition, noise suppression, echo cancellation, beamforming, and automatic command recognition.

points.name: Mozilla Common Voice
points.description: Open-source initiative crowdsourcing multilingual voice recordings to provide public datasets for training speech recognition models.
points.bullets:
A non-profit data provider that builds and releases open-source, multilingual speech datasets for training automatic speech recognition, speech translation, and text-to-speech models. It crowdsources multilingual voice clips and corresponding text data from global volunteer contributors and provides the data freely under a public domain license for developers and enterprises. The organization also builds an API for data retrieval and contribution, alongside a platform for communities to host their own datasets.
1. A data provider that builds crowdsourced speech datasets and a developer API, distributed as open-source data and cloud services for developers and technology companies.
2. A global crowdsourcing platform and public API that collects, validates, and structures multilingual voice clips with associated text and demographic metadata.
3. It delivers large-scale, validated multilingual speech corpora, including diverse accents, acoustic environments, and demographic metadata for training speech recognition, speech-to-text, and deepfake detection models.
4. Customers access the datasets as open-source downloads and will retrieve or contribute data through a cloud API.
5. The data is used to train automatic speech recognition engines, text-to-speech models, speech translation systems, deepfake detectors, and voice-enabled applications for underserved languages.
6. The organization provides data to major technology companies, researchers, and developers building speech and audio models.
7. Its datasets are used by technology companies and researchers to train and test speech recognition and synthesis models.
8. It releases crowdsourced, multilingual speech data entirely under a CC0 license, making it cost and copyright-free for commercial use while focusing extensively on underserved languages.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It is stewarded by the Mozilla Foundation and has received funding from the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit, the UK’s Foreign Commonwealth & Development Office, and Nvidia, with the latter using the data in its open-source speech recognition models.

points.name: University of Salford
points.description: UK university researching acoustics, audio AI, and measurement while building advanced testing facilities.
points.bullets:
A research university and acoustic engineering institution that conducts fundamental research, develops standards, and operates test facilities for acoustics and spatial audio, serving industry partners, government bodies, and students.

2. The organization develops neural networks, including spatially-aware transformers and generative adversarial networks for individual Head-Related Transfer Function upsampling, alongside hybrid boundary element and finite difference time domain numerical techniques.
3. It delivers spatial audio rendering, individualized HRTF prediction, speech intelligibility prediction for hearing aids, soundscape standardization, and sound quality metrics.
4. Customers and partners access its work through collaborative research, licensed algorithms, published standards, and physical testing in anechoic chambers and building environment testing suites.
5. The research and testing apply to hearing aids, home audio rendering, electric vehicles, aeroplane engines, loudspeaker stacks, and light electric vehicles.
6. Customers include product sound engineers, equipment manufacturers, micromobility operators, government bodies, standards organizations, and students.
7. Its research outputs, algorithms, and testing facilities are integrated by industry partners into commercial products and government regulations.
8. The organization combines fundamental psychoacoustic and spatial audio AI research with over sixty years of standards development and heavy-duty physical acoustic testing capabilities.

points.description: US AI startup tracking coughs from ambient sound using on-device microphones.

1. An AI model developer whose cough detection models run entirely on-device on microphone-enabled consumer hardware.
2. A machine-learning engine and patented AI architecture using binary classifiers trained on a massive dataset of real-world cough samples.
3. Continuous cough detection, classification, and counting from ambient sound.
4. Models running on customers' devices, along with data platforms and clinical trial endpoints.
5. Smartphones, wearables, decentralized clinical trials, and consumer disease education efforts.
6. Pharmaceutical companies, medical researchers, government agencies, healthcare providers, and patients.

8. It analyzes the temporal patterns and frequency of continuous coughing rather than the acoustic properties of individually elicited coughs in controlled environments.

Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Software licenses, data provision, clinical trial endpoints, and milestone payments and royalties from prescription digital therapeutics.

points.description: Munich-based R&D center and Lawo subsidiary developing RAVENNA, an open standard for transporting real-time audio over IP networks in broadcast environments.
points.bullets:
A standards body that develops and promotes an open-technology standard for real-time audio and media transport over IP networks for professional broadcast and audio manufacturers. It establishes interoperability specifications using standard networking protocols to enable low-latency, reliable signal distribution. The organization operates as a development support arm helping equipment makers achieve broad industry standard compatibility.
1. A standards body that develops networking specifications and protocols which it provides openly to manufacturers to implement in their own audio products.
2. Network protocols operating at Layer 3 of the OSI model utilizing RTP/RTCP, PTPv2, and DNS to route high-resolution, low-latency media data.
3. Low-latency, fully transparent, high-resolution audio signal distribution scaling up to 192 kHz PCM and 384 kHz DSD/DXD at 24-bit depth.
4. Open-technology standards and specifications provided without a proprietary licensing policy for manufacturers to build into their equipment.
5. In-house signal distribution, live event setups, outside broadcast support, inter-studio WAN links, and large-scale commercial AV installations.
6. Professional audio and broadcast manufacturers, as well as networking infrastructure companies.
7. Its specifications are implemented by equipment makers and networking hardware providers into professional broadcast and AV products.
8. It provides a cost-effective, open route for audio manufacturers to achieve AES67 and SMPTE ST 2110 compatibility without proprietary licensing restrictions.

points.description: Silicon Valley semiconductor company designing high-efficiency amplifier chips for audio equipment.
points.bullets:
A fabless semiconductor company that designed and manufactured Class-D audio amplifier chips, marketing its proprietary digital power processing and digital pulse conversion technology under a branded amplifier class to audio equipment manufacturers.
1. A chip company that designs and sells high-efficiency Class-D audio amplifier semiconductors for integration into consumer audio hardware.
2. The core technology comprises digital power processing and digital pulse conversion algorithms implemented in silicon to switch audio signals at high efficiency approaching 90 percent.
3. The chips deliver high-fidelity audio amplification with high power efficiency, enabling compact amplifier designs without large heat sinks.
4. The organization provides its technology as finished semiconductor components sold to audio equipment manufacturers.
5. The semiconductors are used in budget and consumer audio amplifiers designed for casual, near-field listening.
6. The company sells its semiconductor components to consumer electronics brands and audio equipment manufacturers.
7. Its amplifier chips are designed into compact consumer amplifiers and budget audiophile hardware by equipment brands.
8. The approach distinguishes itself by combining high efficiency with a sound quality characterized by deep low-end response and smooth high frequencies that remained respected among audio enthusiasts.

2. Analog and hybrid electronic circuitry, including variable wave-shape oscillators, unijunction transistor waveshapers, envelope generators, loop recorders, pseudo-random voltage sources, and wideband radio receivers capturing electromagnetic fields from hertz to gigahertz.

points.name: Uncharted Labs
points.description: US startup developing generative AI platforms that create fully produced songs from text prompts.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer whose generative music models run in the cloud behind an API, providing a text-to-music platform that synthesizes fully produced songs from text prompts for consumers, enterprises, and developers.
1. An AI model developer whose generative music models run in the cloud behind an API and as a web application.
2. The core technology combines natural language processing, diffusion models adapted for musical audio, and transformer architectures to convert text prompts into 48 kilohertz stereo audio, using a compression model that encodes audio into discrete tokens and decodes them back into full-resolution waveforms.
3. It delivers text-to-music generation, custom lyrics generation, audio inpainting, stem separation, voice cloning, multilingual vocal support, and MIDI export.
4. Customers access the technology through a web application and a cloud API.
5. Its outputs are used in gaming, advertising, and media production industries.
6. It sells to consumers, developers, and enterprise clients.
7. Its models are accessed directly by end-users and integrated by enterprise clients into their own products.
8. It distinguishes itself by operating a licensed, walled-garden ecosystem that uses filter and fingerprinting technologies for attribution and restricts off-platform distribution of generated content.

Capabilities: AI-powered camera framing, zero-lag whiteboarding, ceiling microphone audio capture and unified video conferencing.
How it is delivered: Finished hardware devices accompanied by proprietary operating system software and firmware updates.
Used in: Enterprise conference rooms, huddle spaces and unified communication meeting rooms.
Sells to: Enterprises standardizing on dedicated collaboration hardware for their meeting spaces.
Value chain: Its finished hardware and software are deployed directly into enterprise conference rooms by organizations.
Differentiator: Its devices run a proprietary operating system while maintaining certification for multiple third-party video conferencing platforms.

points.bullets:

It provides cloud communication services and APIs for contact-center and cloud communications customers rather than meeting-room hardware buyers.

2. Customers get it as cloud-based APIs and services.
3. It is used in contact centers and enterprise voice deployments.
4. It sells to enterprises and contact-center operators.
5. Its platform is deployed directly by enterprises for customer experience operations.

points.name: Nokia — MPEG-I Immersive Audio
points.description: Nokia contributes core rendering technology and standardization work to the MPEG-I immersive audio standard for VR/AR audio experiences, a separate consumer/XR market from cellular voice calls.
points.bullets:
A multinational telecommunications company contributing core spatial rendering technology and standardization work to the MPEG-I immersive audio standard for VR and AR audio experiences. It develops rendering algorithms and evaluation software tools for consumer mobile devices targeting extended reality applications.
1. A technology contributor whose spatial audio rendering algorithms and reference software are contributed to industry standards and run on consumer mobile devices.
2. Spatial audio rendering algorithms, including late reverberation rendering, augmented reality support, and rendering of multiple higher-order ambisonics captures.
3. Immersive audio rendering, late reverberation, augmented reality audio support, and higher-order ambisonics capture rendering for extended reality environments.
4. Baseline technology, core experiments, and evaluation software tools contributed to standardized immersive audio specifications.
5. VR and AR headsets, consumer mobile devices, and 6G extended reality audio experiences.
6. Standards bodies, extended reality device makers, and mobile network operators.
7. Its core rendering technology is standardized and integrated into mobile devices and extended reality platforms by consumer electronics brands.
8. Contributes baseline technology and standardization work directly to the MPEG-I immersive audio standard while researching early-adopter feedback for mobile rendering.

points.name: ByteDance — Doubao
points.description: ByteDance's large language model platform powering conversational voice assistants and real-time voice agents.
points.bullets:
A large language model developer that builds a core conversational AI platform powering real-time voice agents and voice assistants for enterprises and automakers.
1. An AI model developer whose large language models and voice agent capabilities run in the cloud behind an API.
2. Large language models and full-duplex real-time conversational processing algorithms running in the cloud.
3. Real-time conversational voice interaction, full-duplex voice agent response, and voice command processing.
4. Cloud APIs and large language models deployed within real-time conversational voice agent stacks.
5. In-car voice assistants and real-time voice agent systems.
6. Automakers and enterprises deploying conversational assistants.
7. Its cloud models are integrated by automakers into their in-car voice assistant platforms.
8. Full-duplex conversational processing reduces false responses and talk-overs compared to half-duplex voice agent systems.

points.name: ByteDance — Seed Audio
points.description: ByteDance's Seed research team develops audio generation and processing models including scene generation, codecs, and music generation.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer that builds generative audio and neural codec models and releases them as open models for researchers and developers.

2. Neural networks for generative audio synthesis, video-to-music semantic alignment and neural audio codecs.
3. Audio scene generation, dialogue timestamp pinning, video-to-music generation and transparent neural audio coding.
4. Open neural network models released publicly.
5. Generative audio research, video soundtracks and audio compression pipelines.
6. AI researchers and software developers.
7. Its open models are adopted and adapted by developers and researchers building generative audio applications.

clusters.name: Broadcast & Immersive Audio Standards
clusters.description: These organizations develop, certify, or license audio technology standards, formats, and patents rather than producing finished products themselves.

clusters.name: Analog Studio Outboard Gear
clusters.description: These companies manufacture the mixing consoles, outboard processors, interfaces, and microphones that recording and mastering studios buy and use.

clusters.name: Hearing Aids & Cochlear Implants
clusters.description: These companies design and manufacture hearing aids, OTC hearing devices, and cochlear implants as finished medical/consumer products.

clusters.name: Speech Recognition Platforms
clusters.description: These entities build speech recognition, speech synthesis, and voice agent AI models and APIs sold to developers and enterprises building voice-enabled applications.

clusters.name: Hi-Fi Amplifiers & DACs
clusters.description: These companies design and manufacture premium home and studio audio equipment—amplifiers, DACs, streamers, processors, and headphone gear—for audiophile and home-theater consumers.

clusters.name: Touring Line Array Loudspeakers
clusters.description: These companies manufacture loudspeakers, amplifiers, and PA systems for installed and touring live sound reinforcement.

clusters.name: Guitar Amps & Amp Modelers
clusters.description: These companies build guitar/bass amp modeling hardware and software, effects processors, and related plugins for musicians.

clusters.name: MEMS Microphone Suppliers
clusters.description: These companies design and manufacture MEMS microphone chips sold as components into smartphones, wearables, automotive, and consumer electronics brands.

clusters.name: Assistive Listening Systems
clusters.description: These companies build hearing loop and wireless assistive-listening systems (often Auracast-based) that link public venues and devices to hearing aids for accessibility.

clusters.name: Audiophile Home Loudspeakers
clusters.description: These companies design and manufacture finished loudspeakers, soundbars, and subwoofers for home audio and home theater use.

clusters.name: Digital Audio Workstations
clusters.description: These companies develop DAW software (and closely tied plugins/effects) used by musicians and producers to record, edit, and mix music.

clusters.name: Always-On Audio AI Chips
clusters.description: These companies design low-power chips, cores, and processors (often with embedded AI/DSP) that run always-on voice, sound, and audio inference directly on edge devices.

clusters.name: Conferencing Audio Equipment
clusters.description: These companies manufacture headsets, speakerphones, microphones, and room/video systems for video and audio conferencing in business and UC environments.

clusters.name: Live Sound Mixers & PA Gear
clusters.description: These companies design and manufacture mixing consoles, microphones, loudspeakers, and signal processors for professional live sound reinforcement and installed audio systems.

clusters.name: Speech & Audio Datasets
clusters.description: These organizations collect, license, or crowdsource audio and speech recordings used as training data for AI speech and audio models.

clusters.name: OTC Hearing Device Makers
clusters.description: These companies design, manufacture, and sell hearing aids and over-the-counter hearing devices (and related hearables) directly to consumers with hearing loss.

clusters.name: Custom In-Ear Monitors
clusters.description: These companies make finished headphones and in-ear monitor products, primarily custom-fit or premium IEMs for musicians and audio enthusiasts.

clusters.name: Wireless Home Speakers & Soundbars
clusters.description: These companies design and sell finished consumer audio products—smart speakers, headphones/earbuds, and home sound systems—directly to end users.

clusters.name: Custom Install Loudspeakers
clusters.description: These companies design and build loudspeakers and speaker systems for home audio, studio monitoring, custom installation, and automotive use.

clusters.name: On-Device Audio AI Models
clusters.description: These organizations develop AI/ML models and software for understanding and processing voice and audio — spanning speech recognition, synthesis, separation, and sound event detection — designed to run efficiently on-device or at the edge for device makers and app developers.

clusters.name: Automotive Audio Systems
clusters.description: These companies design and supply integrated or branded sound systems built into vehicles, from OEM infotainment audio to premium in-car brand partnerships.

clusters.name: Audio Plugin Developers
clusters.description: These companies develop audio plugins and software (effects, instrument modeling, restoration, pitch correction) for music production, mixing, and mastering.

clusters.name: Studio Condenser & Ribbon Microphones
clusters.description: These entities design and manufacture professional condenser, dynamic, and ribbon microphones for studio recording, live sound, and broadcast use.

clusters.name: Hardware Synthesizers & Samplers
clusters.description: These organizations build synthesizers, electronic instruments, and modeling-based tools that recreate or generate musical sounds for musicians and producers.

clusters.name: Spatial Audio Algorithms
clusters.description: These organizations develop spatial and immersive audio technology—algorithms, software, and simulation tools—that is licensed or integrated into headphones, speakers, games, and live venues rather than sold as a standalone finished product.

clusters.name: Wireless Microphone Systems
clusters.description: These companies make professional microphones and wireless mic/RF systems used in broadcast, live sound, and content creation.

clusters.name: Pro Amplifiers & System Processors
clusters.description: These companies design and manufacture amplifiers, DSPs, mixers, and networked audio gear used for live sound reinforcement and fixed installed-sound systems in venues, retail, and commercial spaces.

clusters.name: Broadcast Consoles & Audio-over-IP
clusters.description: These companies design and manufacture digital mixing consoles and networked audio infrastructure for live sound, broadcast, and install production environments.

clusters.name: Audio Codec Standards & Licensing
clusters.description: These organizations develop, standardize, or license audio codec technology and essential patents used by device makers across the wireless and mobile ecosystem.

clusters.name: Generative Music & Audio AI
clusters.description: These companies build AI models that generate, synthesize, or transform music, speech, and sound content from text or audio prompts.

clusters.name: Speaker Driver Manufacturers
clusters.description: These companies design and manufacture loudspeaker drivers and transducers sold to audio equipment makers across home, pro, automotive, and musical instrument markets.

clusters.name: Budget Hearing Aid Manufacturing
clusters.description: These entities design and produce hearing aids and OTC hearing devices, the finished products purchased by end users for hearing assistance.

clusters.name: Audio DSP Algorithm Licensing
clusters.description: These companies develop and license digital signal processing algorithms—voice front-end capture, room/speaker correction, spatial audio rendering, and automotive sound tuning—that device makers and automakers embed into their own branded products rather than selling finished audio gear themselves.

clusters.name: Academic Acoustics & Hearing Research
clusters.description: These are university and research-institute labs developing AI and acoustic methods for source separation, sound event detection, contextual/selective hearing, and hearing-aid algorithms, rather than companies shipping finished audio products.

clusters.name: Music Production Hardware
clusters.description: Members design DAWs, mixing consoles, audio interfaces, outboard processors, and instrument/effects plugins used by recording and live sound professionals.

clusters.name: Wireless Audio SoCs
clusters.description: These companies design semiconductor chips—converters, codecs, DSPs, amplifiers, and wireless SoCs—that power audio capture, processing, and playback in other companies' devices.

clusters.name: Miniature Speakers & Receivers
clusters.description: These companies manufacture the miniature acoustic transducers—MEMS microphones, speaker drivers, balanced-armature receivers, bone-conduction and solid-state microspeakers—that device makers integrate into earbuds, hearables, and hearing aids.

clusters.name: Public Address & Paging Systems
clusters.description: These companies manufacture commercial installed-sound equipment—speakers, amplifiers, and conferencing systems—for public address, paging, and voice evacuation in venues, schools, and transit spaces.

clusters.name: Guitar Effects Pedal Makers
clusters.description: These companies design and manufacture guitar/bass effects pedals and multi-effects processors using instrument modeling and DSP for musicians.

clusters.name: Studio Monitor Speakers
clusters.description: These companies design and manufacture amplifiers, studio monitors, speaker drivers, and signal processors used in professional installed and live sound audio systems.

clusters.name: Source Separation & Voice Cleanup
clusters.description: These companies build AI software that isolates, separates, or cleans individual voices and instrument stems from mixed audio for musicians and call/meeting participants.

clusters.name: Speech Synthesis & Voice Agent Models
clusters.description: These organizations develop AI models for text-to-speech, voice cloning, and real-time conversational speech-to-speech agents.

clusters.name: Acoustic Test & Measurement Systems
clusters.description: These members build audio analyzers, measurement microphones, acoustic chambers, and room/simulation tools used to test and characterize transducers and sound quality.

clusters.name: True Wireless Earbuds
clusters.description: Finished-product makers of headphones, earbuds, and hearables sold directly to consumers, often adding ANC and personalized hearing features.

clusters.name: Venue & Architectural Loudspeakers
clusters.description: These companies design and manufacture professional loudspeaker systems, amplifiers, and signal processors used for live sound reinforcement and permanent venue installations.

clusters.name: Stage PA Speakers & Amplifiers
clusters.description: These companies build amplifiers, speakers, mixers, and related audio gear for live sound reinforcement and fixed installation markets.

clusters.name: Audio Interfaces & Converters
clusters.description: These companies build professional audio interfaces, converters, mixing consoles, and networked audio systems for recording studios, live sound, and installed AV.

clusters.name: Premium Wireless Headphones
clusters.description: These are companies that design and manufacture finished headphones, earbuds, and related personal/home audio products for consumers.

clusters.name: AV Receivers & Music Streamers
clusters.description: These companies design and sell finished consumer home-audio equipment—AV receivers, amplifiers, and networked multiroom speakers—for home entertainment and listening systems.

clusters.name: Audio Amplifier Chips
clusters.description: These companies design and manufacture amplifier, converter, codec, and related DSP/SoC chips that power audio in other companies' finished products.

tag_info.hearing_assistive_links: Provides connectivity for hearing aids and assistive listening such as ASHA, telecoil, or broadcast audio

tag_info.active_noise_cancellation: Develops active noise cancellation and transparency technology for headphones
tag_info.spatial_immersive_audio: Develops spatial or immersive audio formats, renderers, or technology
tag_info.personalized_hearing_profiles: Develops personalized HRTF or hearing-profile audio personalization, including HRTFs estimated from photos or calibration
tag_info.room_speaker_correction: Develops room acoustics or loudspeaker correction and tuning software
tag_info.automotive_sound_software: Develops in-car sound processing such as road noise cancellation, sound zones, or vehicle tuning
tag_info.loudness_broadcast_processing: Develops loudness management or broadcast audio processing
tag_info.game_audio_middleware: Develops game or interactive audio engines and middleware
tag_info.dsp_dev_frameworks: Provides frameworks or tools for developing audio DSP software
tag_info.speech_recognition: Develops speech-to-text recognition models or services
tag_info.speech_synthesis_voice_cloning: Develops text-to-speech, voice synthesis, or voice cloning
tag_info.voice_agents_speech_to_speech: Develops real-time conversational voice agents or speech-to-speech models, including full-duplex dialogue models that listen while speaking and handle interruptions
tag_info.generative_music_sound: Develops AI that generates music or sound effects
tag_info.source_separation_enhancement: Develops AI source separation, stem extraction, or speech and audio enhancement
tag_info.sound_event_detection: Develops AI that detects sound events or classifies acoustic scenes
tag_info.contextual_audio: Builds devices or AI that perceive the acoustic world around the user (who is speaking, from where), infer intent, or selectively reshape what the user hears
tag_info.neural_audio_codecs: Develops neural audio codecs or audio tokenizers, for compression or as the token vocabulary of generative audio models
tag_info.on_device_audio_models: Develops compact speech or audio models built to run on-device: small ASR, distilled or quantized speech models for NPUs and edge hardware
tag_info.neural_dsp: Replaces classic audio DSP with neural networks: neural echo cancellation, beamforming, dereverberation, differentiable DSP, or neural speaker protection
tag_info.audio_video_generation: Develops AI that generates audio for video or jointly with video: video-to-audio Foley, AI sound effects for picture, or speech-driven lip-sync and facial animation
tag_info.generated_audio_evaluation: Develops metrics, benchmarks, or services that evaluate the quality of AI-generated or neurally coded audio
tag_info.music_analysis_transcription: Develops AI that transcribes or analyzes music: notes, chords, beats, structure, or playing technique, or attributes music to training data
tag_info.paralinguistic_analysis: Develops AI that reads how something is said rather than what: emotion, prosody, speaking style, or speaker traits
tag_info.audio_language_models: Develops audio-language or audio foundation models that reason about sound and speech
tag_info.industrial_acoustic_monitoring: Uses acoustic or vibration analysis to monitor industrial machines
tag_info.audio_identification_security: Provides audio fingerprinting, watermarking, provenance or signed capture, or synthetic-speech, deepfake, anti-spoofing, and voice-fraud detection
tag_info.embedded_audio_ml_tooling: Provides tools for building and deploying audio ML models on embedded devices

tag_info.audio_interfaces_converters: Makes audio interfaces or studio converters
tag_info.outboard_processors: Makes outboard studio processing hardware such as reverbs, compressors, or effects
tag_info.audio_plugins: Develops audio effect or instrument plugins
tag_info.install_live_sound: Makes installed or live sound systems, loudspeakers, or system DSP
tag_info.conferencing_audio: Makes conferencing audio products such as microphone arrays or meeting-room systems
tag_info.instrument_modeling_effects: Makes instrument amp modeling, effects pedals, or musical instrument processors
tag_info.audio_odm_manufacturing: Contract manufactures or designs audio products for other brands
tag_info.smart_speakers_home_audio: Makes smart speakers, home audio, or hi-fi products
tag_info.otc_hearing_devices: Makes over-the-counter hearing devices or hearing features in consumer earbuds
tag_info.cochlear_implants: Makes cochlear implants or implantable hearing systems
tag_info.automotive_audio_systems: Supplies complete automotive audio systems to carmakers
tag_info.audio_analyzers: Makes audio analyzers and electroacoustic test systems
tag_info.transducer_measurement: Makes loudspeaker or transducer measurement systems
tag_info.acoustic_test_psychoacoustics: Provides acoustic test equipment, measurement microphones, or psychoacoustic analysis
tag_info.acoustic_chambers: Builds anechoic chambers or acoustic test facilities
tag_info.acoustic_simulation: Provides acoustic or room simulation software, including synthetic audio training data
tag_info.audio_standards_bodies: Standards body or industry association that defines audio standards
tag_info.audio_patent_licensing: Runs audio patent pools or licenses audio patents and technology
tag_info.audio_certification: Runs an audio product certification or logo program
tag_info.audio_datasets: Provides audio or speech datasets or audio data-collection services
tag_info.medical_acoustics: Applies audio sensing to medicine, such as digital stethoscopes or cough and voice biomarkers
tag_info.gunshot_public_safety: Provides gunshot detection or acoustic public-safety systems
tag_info.ultrasonic_sensing: Uses ultrasound for presence, gesture, or proximity sensing
